title: Renaming into another top’s alias silently changes geological identity
current: The rename path checks existing canonical names but deletes a matching alias without checking its owner. Adding an alias uses ON CONFLICT(alias) DO UPDATE and can transfer another definition’s alias. The manager checks only canonical-name clashes, so this can happen without a merge confirmation.
evidence: top-ui-batch-evidence.json: using the actual Global FM Tops Manager, A at MD 100 and B at MD 1000, with B alias “B old”, renaming A to “B old” changes the same untouched Map source from 1000 to 100. merge_confirmation_calls = 0. top-identity-evidence.json independently demonstrates alias transfer through add_top_alias.
impact: A legacy name can silently identify a different geological horizon. A Map/grid source or import referencing that alias then selects a different top despite no user-controlled geological merge. This is demonstrated material geological misidentification, not a numerical-equation discrepancy.
scenario: A project contains a legacy vendor name for one formation. A user gives a different formation that name in the manager; subsequent top-based mapping uses the other pick. The evidence is synthetic; no client incident is alleged.
fix: Resolve both canonical-name and alias ownership before changing either. Reject a different owner or route through the existing explicit merge confirmation. Never delete/reassign another definition’s alias as a side effect of rename.
tests: Actual manager rename and Other Names collision tests; unchanged Map source must retain its original pick; verify import resolution, both definitions’ picks, source/notes and aliases before and after reopen.

title: A reader can consume a live writer’s staged grid and trigger an inconsistent rollback
current: save commits the new database row before promoting the staged file. load treats a matching stage as crash recovery and moves it into place. If a live reader does this first, the writer cannot find its stage, reports failure and restores the old database row, while the already-promoted new file remains.
evidence: grid-reader-publication-evidence.json: two real project connections, with an ordered reader at the post-commit/pre-promote boundary. The reader loads 9000 m; writer raises FileNotFoundError; database row reverts to ft and old updated_at, but reopened file still holds 9000 m and the new notes. No real process kill is required for this race.
impact: A failed save can remain partly accepted, and database metadata disagrees with the scientific file. Subsequent operations cannot rely on rollback restoring the previous accepted grid. Probability was not measured; the interleaving is deterministic and reachable with concurrent project sessions.
scenario: Map or another session loads a grid just as a save has committed its row but has not promoted its file.
fix: Give publication/recovery a shared ownership or locking protocol spanning commit and promotion. Recovery must distinguish an active writer, and rollback must not restore an old row after another participant has accepted its publication. Preserve the existing before/after-commit crash recovery.
tests: Use a barrier with two connections or processes at commit/promote. Assert save outcome, row/file units, versions, geometry and values agree. Repeat for insert/update/rename and retain kill-before/after-commit tests.

title: Bulk and mapped alias imports repeatedly duplicate the same canonical pick
current: Import duplicate checks compare the normalized input name literally. The insert trigger subsequently resolves aliases to the canonical definition/name. An alias therefore misses an already-present canonical row on every import.
evidence: import-alias-evidence.json: actual XLSX bulk and CSV mapped import_all calls, existing Canonical pick MD 100 source XON and alias Legacy. Import Legacy once gives two identical canonical rows; repeating gives three. Both paths report no errors; all rows retain the same well/definition/MD/source.
impact: Imports are not idempotent for supported aliases. Redundant picks inflate records, exports and displays and can interfere with later uniqueness-sensitive editing. This does not create a second definition and does not by itself prove an EUR or volumetric error.
scenario: A client reimports a vendor tops file using an old name after a canonical rename. Each repeat adds another copy of the same pick.
fix: Resolve the input top to its canonical identity before duplicate detection in each importer, including dynamic-top columns. Apply the current well/depth/source policy to that identity; retain genuinely distinct repeated crossings and provenance.
tests: Actual bulk/mapped/dynamic-column imports using canonical and alias spellings, repeat import, mixed case/spacing, same MD and different sources, distinct MDs and reopen. Assert exact row counts and unchanged unrelated headers/locations.

title: Deleting a migrated Correlation-only top is undone on project reopen
current: Each project open reads legacy correlation:tops entries marked added and recreates missing definitions. Deleting the global definition removes its picks/aliases but leaves that legacy creation intent in project metadata.
evidence: top-ui-batch-evidence.json: actual manager deletion removes Corr-only before close; ProjectDatabase reopen recreates Corr-only. top-identity-evidence.json provides a minimal database reproduction.
impact: An intentional delete does not persist for this supported legacy-project population. The recreated definition is empty; deleted picks are not recovered. This is not a request to add source-deletion UI.
scenario: An older project has a top created in Correlation. Its migrated global top is deleted, then returns after the next open.
fix: Make legacy creation backfill one-time or explicitly retire its creation metadata when the user deletes the canonical definition. Preserve unrelated Correlation styles and do not recreate deliberately deleted definitions.
tests: Migrate an old Correlation-added top, delete through the manager, close and reopen twice; verify absence and preservation of all unrelated picks, definitions, aliases and module settings.

title: An open Batch Calculations window cannot resolve a top renamed elsewhere
current: Persistent batch definitions are retargeted correctly, but an already-open tab retains its original top text. Calculation compares that text with fresh canonical pick names without resolving aliases.
evidence: top-ui-batch-evidence.json: the live dialog calculates GROSS 80 ft / NET 20 ft before rename. After Haynesville → Haynesville New, its old name remains a valid project alias and the saved definition is correct, yet the live definition raises Skip: no Haynesville pick (zone top). Reloading the definition restores the same numerical results.
impact: A normal cross-module rename interrupts a valid batch workflow until it is refreshed. No incorrect published numerical values were demonstrated in this reproduction.
scenario: Batch is left open while a top is renamed in the global manager, then the user runs the existing batch definition.
fix: Resolve zone boundary names against canonical project identities at the database-aware calculation entry and refresh held UI definitions when relevant top revisions change. Avoid changing geological boundary selection or formulas.
tests: Open a batch tab, rename/merge a boundary in another connected window, run without reopening; test both top/base boundaries and a typed valid alias, preserving source selection and expected outputs.

title: Protected-source enforcement misses embedded data ZIPs and nested archives
current: The scanner extracts PYZ and CArchive type Z ZIP entries, but not ordinary type x data ZIP payloads. ZIP member names are checked without recursively inspecting contained archives. Package/name matching is case-sensitive.
evidence: protection-matrix-evidence.json uses actual PyInstaller CArchive/PYZ writers: protected source inside a type x embedded ZIP passes customer and owner checks, as does a nested ZIP; OGCORE/FORMULAS.PY is missed. Positive controls catch all 27 tested suffix/depth variants, loose ZIP/egg/whl/PYZ, type Z, module/package/script entries, missing extensions and unreadable executables.
impact: The release gate cannot substantiate its stated “no protected source in embedded ZIPs” guarantee. This is a verified checker gap, not evidence that the actual current package leaks source. Both actual Linux customer/owner builds passed the checker and independent source-oriented inventory. Fixture extension files are presence controls, not runnable binaries.
scenario: A dependency or data collection rule adds a ZIP as ordinary PyInstaller data or wraps one inside another archive; a release with protected content can be accepted.
fix: Inspect archive-like embedded data by content/name, recurse with bounded depth/size, and normalize relevant path spelling for the supported platform. Keep unreadable archive failures closed and retain clean-package positive controls.
tests: Add real type x data ZIP, nested ZIP/PYZ, base_library.zip and Windows case variants to customer and owner negative fixtures; assert nonzero exit. Run the same checks on actual Windows artifacts.
